title: Third-Party Integration Audit, Access, and Retention Policy
author: Priya Patel
content:
Summary

This policy defines mandatory controls and end-to-end procedures for onboarding, operating, and decommissioning third-party integrations (3P connectors, vendor APIs, partner systems) with respect to access control (RBAC), authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC checks, incident response integration, and compliance evidence collection. It applies to all product and infrastructure integrations that exchange or access Redwood Inference customer or production data.

Scope

- In-scope: any integration that reads, writes, proxies, or requests metadata from production services, including SaaS connectors, hosted vendor agents, and partner-managed webhooks.
- Out-of-scope: internal tools that never connect to customer or production data channels (documented exceptions require risk approval).

Goals and non-goals

- Goals: ensure least-privilege access, consistent audit trail and immutable evidence, clear retention and data residency mapping, fast investigative workflows for incidents, and defensible compliance posture for audits (SOC2/ISO).
- Non-goals: prescribe vendor procurement decisions or pricing; those remain with Finance/Procurement.

Roles and responsibilities

- Security (owner): policy custodian; approves security evidence packages; runs periodic sampling reviews.
- Integrations/Product (requester/owner): submit onboarding package, implement required logging hooks, maintain connector config.
- Eng-Infra (ops): configure audit collectors, retention enforcement, and secure network egress controls.
- Legal/Compliance: define preservation holds, retention overrides for legal requests.

Authentication and RBAC requirements

1. Minimized privileged identities
- All third-party integrations must use dedicated service identities (no shared human credentials).
- Each connector gets a unique long-lived client-id and short-lived credential pattern when supported (preferred: OIDC + short-lived TLS or mTLS).

2. Authorization model
- Integrations are assigned one of three roles: read-only, write-limited, or admin-proxy. Default is read-only.
- Role mapping is configured via the authz-service and enforced at the API gateway level (authz-service policy id: AZ-THIRD-PARTY-01).

3. Approval and attestation
- Every new integration requires approval from the owning product manager and security; approval recorded in the integration registry (registry ticket ID required).
- Quarterly attestation: owners must re-affirm the necessity and RBAC scope of active integrations.

Audit logging requirements

- All integration activity must emit structured audit events to the centralized audit pipeline (service name: audit-collector). Required fields: timestamp, service, connector_id, actor, action, resource, request_id, source_ip, success/failure, change_summary (free text max 1024 chars).

- Logging format (JSON example)
{
  "timestamp": "2026-01-01T12:00:00Z",
  "service": "ingest-api",
  "connector_id": "stripe-sync-abc123",
  "actor": "svc-thirdparty-stripe",
  "action": "create_customer",
  "resource": "customer:cus_9z8y",
  "request_id": "req-6b4f",
  "source_ip": "203.0.113.42",
  "success": true,
  "change_summary": "created customer with email redacted@example.com"
}

- SLOs and availability
- Audit events must arrive at audit-collector within 30s for 99% of events. Missing or delayed telemetry must trigger an integration health alert routed to #integrations-ops.

- Tamper-resistance
- Raw audit streams are append-only and backed by immutable object storage (WORM) for high-sensitivity connectors when required by policy. All logs are signed with a rotating key via KMS to provide provenance.

Data residency and retention matrix

- Default retention policy (applies unless overridden by contract or legal hold):

Table: retention matrix
Service / Log type | Typical retention | Minimum retention | Encryption | Owner
authz-service (access grants) | 365 days | 90 days | AES-256 + KMS | security
audit-collector (structured events) | 2 years | 1 year | AES-256 + KMS | eng-infra
request-traces (full traces/spans) | 90 days | 30 days | AES-256 at rest | eng-platform
third-party-payloads (raw vendor payloads) | 180 days | 30 days | Customer-region KMS | integrations/product
compliance-evidence-bundles | 7 years | 3 years | AES-256 + HSM-wrapped keys | compliance

- Residency mapping
- Integrations must declare the geographic regions where data will be stored or transmitted during onboarding. For EU/UK customer data, default storage must be in eu-* regions unless contractually waived.

- Cross-border replication
- Cross-region replication of logs or payloads is allowed only with documented business justification and signed data processing addendums. Replication requests require security and legal approval and are tracked in the registry.

Secure SDLC controls for connector code

- All code shipped by Redwood that interfaces with third-party vendors (connectors, agents) must follow these checks before production deployment:
  1. Static application security testing (SAST) pass with zero critical findings.
  2. Dependency vulnerability policy: no unpatched critical CVEs; high-severity must have documented mitigation and scheduled patch window.
  3. Secrets scanning: no hard-coded secrets in repo or builds.
  4. Integration tests that exercise happy and failure paths for auth and error reporting.
  5. Security review: triage within 5 business days; approvals logged in PR and integration registry.

- Third-party vendor-supplied agents installed in customer networks must have a documented SBOM and supported upgrade path; unsupported binaries are disallowed by default.

Incident response and investigation workflow

- Detection and triage
  1. Integration health alerts (failed token refresh, high error rate, missing audit events) are paged to on-call via PagerDuty with severity mapping: SEV2 (service degradation) or SEV1 (suspected data exfiltration).
  2. On-call collects evidence using standardized collector scripts and documents actions in the incident ticket.

- Evidence preservation
  1. Immediately snapshot relevant logs, connector configs, and audit-collector streams to an evidence bucket with legal hold tag.
  2. If exfiltration suspected, engage Legal and Forensics; preserve network captures and, if available, encrypted key manifests.

- Notification and containment
  1. Containment options: rotate connector credentials, revoke tokens at gateway, isolate connector IP ranges, or disable connector at config management. Which action to take is decided by security on-call in consultation with product owner.
  2. Post-containment verification includes ensuring no further unauthorized activity for 24 hours and that audit event arrival returns to baseline.

Compliance evidence workflow (for audits)

- Evidence package components
  - Integration registry export (approved connectors with rationale), role-to-permission maps, audit event extracts (time-bounded), retention policy records, KMS key rotation logs, and attestation records.

- Packaging process (standardized)
  1. Request: Compliance requests evidence via the evidence intake form; security-owner assigns a package owner.
  2. Collection: use the evidence-orch service to pull signed audit slices and attachments into a sealed evidence bundle (bundle id included).
  3. Verification: reviewer checks signatures and manifest; discrepancies trigger a remediation runbook.
  4. Delivery: deliver sealed bundle through the secure transfer mechanism (SFTP with mutual TLS or the compliance portal).

Risk exceptions and temporary access model

- Exception framework
  - Short-lived exceptions (<= 30 days) are recorded with an explicit compensating control (e.g., additional logging, network isolation) and must have a designated approver from Security and Product.
  - Long-lived exceptions (> 30 days) require risk committee review and legally binding justification.

- Emergency temporary access
  1. Security-approved emergency tokens are issued with a maximum lifetime of 8 hours and always require requestor identity and justification logged in the registry.
  2. All emergency tokens are rotated immediately after use and subject to audit.

Operational checklists (onboarding, decommissioning)

- Onboarding checklist (product/integrations owner)
  1. Fill integration registry form and indicate data residency.
  2. Obtain security approval and assign RBAC role.
  3. Implement structured audit events and test end-to-end flow to audit-collector.
  4. Confirm retention class and encryption key location.
  5. Run security gating pipeline and get SAST/DAST results.

- Decommissioning checklist
  1. Rotate or revoke credentials and remove egress rules.
  2. Export final audit slice and mark evidence bundle.
  3. Apply retention policy for residual artifacts; if deletion requested, follow secure deletion workflow and record proof.

Appendix A: Example CLI snippets

- Exporting a time-bounded audit slice (example):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $EVIDENCE_TOKEN" \ 
    "https://audit-collector.internal/api/v1/export?connector_id=stripe-sync-abc123&from=2025-12-01T00:00:00Z&to=2025-12-31T23:59:59Z" \ 
    -o stripe-sync-dec-2025-logs.json

- Rotating connector credentials (gateway CLI):
  rwd-gateway rotate-connector --id stripe-sync-abc123 --reason "compromise-suspected" --force

Appendix B: Evidence manifest template (text)

manifest_id: BUNDLE-20260109-0001
created_by: priya.patel@redwood.ai
components:
  - integration_registry_export: path/to/registry.csv
  - audit_slice: path/to/stripe-sync-dec-2025-logs.json
  - kms_rotation_logs: path/to/kms-rotation.log
signature: <base64-signature>

Review cadence and metrics

- Quarterly: sample 10% of active third-party connectors for RBAC and logging completeness.
- Annual: evidence readiness drill (tabletop) with Legal and Compliance.
- KPIs: percentage of integrations with end-to-end structured events (target 100%), average time to produce an evidence bundle (target < 3 business days).

Related documents and references

- See audit-collector onboarding guide, authz-service policy AZ-THIRD-PARTY-01, integration registry template, and secure-sdlc checklist.

Questions and contact

- Policy owner: security@redwood.ai (Priya Patel). For urgent incidents, contact security on-call via PagerDuty (rotations listed in Eng SRE runbook).

Change log

- 2025-09-15: Initial draft and stakeholder review.
- 2025-11-02: Added KMS rotation requirements and retention matrix updates.
- 2026-01-10: Clarified emergency token lifecycle and evidence packaging steps.
